Business.description: What the major business and general-news outlets are leading with.
Business.overview: Coverage this cycle is dominated by the fallout from Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang's resignation amid a Chinese espionage scandal and the run-up to Anthropic's blockbuster IPO, both seen as make-or-break tests for the AI trade. A secondary cluster of outlets is covering Friday's nationwide FAA ground stop and the Microsoft global outage, plus Trump's planned three-way summit with Xi and Putin in Shenzhen.

stories.headline: Jensen Huang's resignation and spy scandal roils Nvidia and Washington
stories.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned after revelations of two extramarital affairs, including one with a woman U.S. intelligence believes was a Chinese intelligence asset tied to Megaspeed, triggering a board investigation, congressional subpoenas and hundreds of billions in market-value losses.

stories.headline: Anthropic prices record-setting IPO amid AI jitters
stories.summary: Anthropic set terms for an IPO that could value the Claude maker near $1.3 trillion and raise up to $90 billion with a concurrent private placement, with trading expected to begin around Nov. 19 just as Nvidia's leadership crisis tests investor confidence in AI.

stories.headline: Nationwide FAA ground stop exposes air traffic control weaknesses
stories.summary: A nationwide ground stop highlighted recurring failures in the FAA's aging air traffic control infrastructure, stranding thousands of passengers and reigniting political blame over delayed upgrades.

stories.headline: Microsoft restores services after day-long global outage
stories.summary: Microsoft said it had fully restored Outlook, Teams and Copilot after a global outage disrupted government agencies, hospitals and police departments worldwide.

stories.headline: Trump to hold unprecedented three-way summit with Xi and Putin
stories.summary: President Trump is set to hold an unprecedented three-way meeting with China's Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin next week in Shenzhen, a summit that will also feature a gathering of U.S. tech CEOs amid a stalled trade war and expanding export controls.

stories.headline: Bessent and Lutnick clash inside Trump administration over Nvidia China curbs
stories.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick are clashing over the Commerce Department's handling of export-control scrutiny on Megaspeed, the company at the center of the Nvidia spy scandal, with Lutnick now facing calls to testify before Congress.

stories.headline: Trump Media faces $1 billion debt crunch as bitcoin bet sours
stories.summary: A plunge in Trump Media's shares and in cryptocurrency prices could force the Truth Social parent to sell assets or take on costly new debt to manage an approaching $1 billion debt obligation.

stories.headline: CVS weighs breaking up its drugstore business
stories.summary: CVS is considering spinning off its drugstore chain, a move unlikely to quiet Washington's criticism of the company but one that could still create value for shareholders according to Wall Street analysts.

Business.gaps: No recent relevant coverage was found from Puck or The Information in this window; WSJ, NYT, FT, The Economist, Politico, Business Insider and BBC coverage is limited to the provided feed items since web search for those outlets is restricted.

US politics.overview: Coverage is dominated by the fallout from Democrats' sweeping midterm wins, especially an intensifying leadership battle between Chuck Schumer and Chris Van Hollen for Senate majority leader, alongside continued fallout from Friday's historic nationwide FAA ground stop and the Jensen Huang/Nvidia scandal's reach into the Trump administration. Outlets are also digging into new political geography revealed by the midterms, a looming Supreme Court asylum case, and a Trump administration land-sale plan drawing bipartisan pushback.

stories.headline: Van Hollen's insurgency against Schumer roils Senate Democrats
stories.summary: Sen. Chris Van Hollen formally announced he will challenge Chuck Schumer for Senate majority leader, arguing voters demanded 'new leadership,' while Schumer insists he already has the votes to keep his post; the secret-ballot election is set for Dec. 1.

stories.headline: FAA ground stop fallout triggers funding and accountability fight
stories.summary: After Friday's roughly four-hour nationwide ground stop—blamed on an overloaded old telecom router during an upgrade by contractor L3Harris—Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and Speaker Mike Johnson are pushing Congress for new air traffic control funding, while officials say there's no evidence of a cyberattack.

stories.headline: Trump economic advisers clash over handling of Nvidia spy-sex scandal
stories.summary: Treasury Secretary blames Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick's department for failing to act on export-control concerns involving Megaspeed, the company at the center of former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair scandal, exposing infighting among Trump's top economic aides.

stories.headline: Democrats' midterm 'avalanche' redraws the political map
stories.summary: Analysis argues last week's Democratic sweep was 'more than a wave, it was an avalanche' that revealed new political contours across the country, a theme echoed in a new Cook Political Report post-election briefing describing the result as the 'Annihilation of the Trump Coalition.'

stories.headline: Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins flips Alaska's governorship
stories.summary: Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins became the first Democrat elected Alaska governor in over two decades, part of a broader Democratic surge that also saw Mary Peltola again claim victory in Alaska's Senate race as vote counting continues.

stories.headline: Supreme Court agrees to hear Trump's asylum suspension case
stories.summary: The Supreme Court will take up a challenge to the Trump administration's 'invasion'-based suspension of asylum at the southern border, a case Roll Call frames as a major test of executive immigration power.

stories.headline: Trump's plan to sell public lands draws bipartisan backlash
stories.summary: The Trump administration's proposal to sell some federal public lands to states, local governments and tribes is drawing swift bipartisan opposition, NPR reports.

stories.headline: Medicaid work-requirement enforcement delayed six months
stories.summary: The Trump administration announced states will get an additional six months—until July—to implement the Medicaid work-requirement provision from Republicans' tax-and-spending law originally set to take effect Jan. 1.

US politics.gaps: Politico, NYT, WSJ and The Guardian block web search so only their provided feed items were used; NOTUS's most recent available items were from earlier in the cycle rather than the last 48 hours.

Tech & AI.overview: Coverage is dominated by the fallout from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's forced resignation over admitted affairs including one with an alleged Chinese spy, and by Anthropic's blockbuster Nasdaq IPO roadshow, which outlets are closely tying to the Huang scandal given Nvidia's planned $10B investment. A secondary story cluster covers Friday's nationwide FAA ground stop caused by an equipment failure, plus continuing scrutiny of AI chip export controls to China.

stories.headline: Jensen Huang ousted as Nvidia CEO after admitted affairs, one with alleged Chinese spy
stories.summary: Nvidia's board accepted the resignation of 33-year CEO Jensen Huang this week after reports he had affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and two other women, including a direct report, with CFO Colette Kress stepping in as interim CEO. Reporting suggests his exit may also trace to the company's risky business practices and possible export-control liability around Chinese chip smuggling.

stories.headline: Anthropic kicks off Wall Street roadshow for record-setting Nasdaq IPO
stories.summary: Anthropic is marketing 825 million Class A shares at $70-$78 each, targeting a fully diluted valuation of roughly $1.4 trillion and aiming to raise up to $90.4 billion including a $26 billion private placement from Google, Nvidia, Microsoft and others; the deal is reportedly oversubscribed and expected to price around November 19 under ticker ANT.

stories.headline: Nvidia's $10B Anthropic IPO pledge draws scrutiny after Huang's exit
stories.summary: Nvidia had agreed to buy about $10 billion of Anthropic shares as part of a $26 billion private placement tied to the IPO, and analysts say Huang's departure and his central role linking the two AI giants now puts that pledge under fresh scrutiny.

stories.headline: Nationwide FAA ground stop traced to copper-to-fiber wiring upgrade gone wrong
stories.summary: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said Friday's hours-long nationwide ground stop, the FAA's third ever, stemmed from a project replacing old copper wiring with fiber at a remote facility, possibly involving a faulty router installed by contractor L3Harris, and he denied any AI involvement.

stories.headline: Chinese AI labs reportedly training on export-banned Nvidia Blackwell chips
stories.summary: A forensic report cited by an ex-OpenAI engineer found evidence of Nvidia's restricted Blackwell chips underpinning models from DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax and Ant Group despite US export controls, adding to pressure on Nvidia amid the Huang fallout.

stories.headline: Italy fines Meta €805 million over Android photo access without consent
stories.summary: Italy's data protection agency fined Meta €805 million for allegedly accessing Android users' photos and videos without informing them or obtaining consent, per a Reuters report aggregated by Techmeme.

stories.headline: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet for agent-based purchases
stories.summary: OpenAI, a company announcement, unveiled ChatGPT Wallet, letting agents in ChatGPT Work, Codex and dots complete purchases with user approval and existing card protections, marking a second attempt at AI-driven shopping after scrapping its earlier Instant Checkout feature, as The Decoder also reported.

stories.headline: Banks shut out Chinese and Hong Kong investors from Anthropic's IPO
stories.summary: Citing Bloomberg reporting, banks are rejecting buy orders for Anthropic's IPO from mainland China and Hong Kong investors due to U.S. export-control rules known as ITAR, underscoring the geopolitical sensitivities wrapped around the listing.

Tech & AI.gaps: VentureBeat and Google DeepMind had no recent (last 48h) coverage found on the AI/Huang/Anthropic storylines; The Verge, Wired, Ars Technica, NYT, WSJ, FT, The Economist and The Guardian were reported only from provided feed items since they block web search.

Energy.overview: Coverage over the last 24-48 hours is dominated by the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, including shrinking climate-finance pledges and UN Secretary-General Guterres's closing remarks, alongside fallout from Nvidia's Jensen Huang stepping down and its implications for the AI-driven data center energy boom. Energy markets news also features prominently, with oil prices swinging on Trump's Iran comments and a historic polar vortex breakdown raising cold-weather risk, while Exxon's legal challenge to EU carbon capture rules and a split U.S. appeals court ruling on California's climate disclosure laws highlight ongoing regulatory fights.

stories.headline: Climate-finance pledges collapse 70% as COP31 opens
stories.summary: Carbon Brief's analysis found that public funding pledged to help developing countries tackle climate change has dropped by more than 70% in 2026, with the US providing no official climate finance and Germany, France and Japan yet to announce new commitments.

stories.headline: UN chief's closing COP31 message: fossil fuels are 'killing our planet'
stories.summary: In what may be his final speech as UN Secretary-General before the climate summit, Antonio Guterres warned that as heat records keep shattering, fossil fuel interests keep profiting "while killing our planet."

stories.headline: Record polar vortex breakdown raises cold weather risk
stories.summary: FT reports that an early collapse of the wind system that normally traps Arctic air is the latest in a string of extreme atmospheric events, raising fresh concerns about severe cold snaps this winter.

stories.headline: Oil prices rebound as Trump questions need for Iran deal
stories.summary: Oil prices swung from losses to gains after President Trump said the U.S. doesn't need a deal with Iran, reinjecting geopolitical risk premium into crude markets.

stories.headline: Jensen Huang's departure throws the AI boom into fresh chaos
stories.summary: Nvidia chief Jensen Huang's resignation is roiling the AI sector just as Meta struck new deals for low-carbon cement and green steel for its data centers, China pushed ahead with small modular reactor startups, and California ordered utilities to plan for virtual power plants.

stories.headline: Exxon sues the EU over carbon capture rules
stories.summary: Exxon Mobil filed a confidential legal challenge to the European Union's carbon capture regulations, described as the latest attempt by the U.S. energy giant to roll back Brussels's green rules, even as Europe's carbon capture capacity is projected to surge by 2035.

stories.headline: California climate disclosure laws survive, partly, after appeals court split
stories.summary: The Ninth Circuit allowed California's SB 253 scope 1 and 2 emissions reporting requirements to proceed while blocking enforcement of scope 3 reporting and the related SB 261 climate-risk disclosure law.

stories.headline: 2026 on track to be the warmest or second-warmest year on record
stories.summary: Carbon Brief's quarterly state-of-the-climate analysis puts 2026 at a 67% chance of surpassing 2024 as the hottest year on record, driven by a rapidly strengthening El Niño, with 2027 now expected to break the record further.

Energy.gaps: Latitude Media and Argus Media could not be checked within the search budget for this report, so no recent coverage from them is reflected here. Reuters, NYT, and The Economist block web search and had no relevant energy/climate feed items provided.

China.description: China politics, economy and business coverage.
China.overview: Coverage across these outlets is dominated by preparations for next week's unprecedented Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral meeting at the APEC summit in Shenzhen, and by the fallout from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation amid an alleged affair and Chinese espionage scandal that is rattling the global AI chip supply chain. Business and tech outlets are also tracking China's surprisingly strong October export data, EV industry product launches, and new corporate moves in China's domestic chip sector.

stories.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin to hold first-ever three-way summit in Shenzhen
stories.summary: The White House confirmed Trump will meet Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin on November 19 on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, with Washington saying it intends to raise nuclear arms reduction and Iran, while avoiding Ukraine; Shenzhen has spent two years on security and infrastructure preparations, banning drones citywide and relocating some residents near the venue.

stories.headline: Jensen Huang's resignation and alleged China spy ties shake AI chip supply chain
stories.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's abrupt exit following revelations of an affair and alleged links to a Chinese intelligence-linked businesswoman is reverberating through China's AI chip supply chain, with Nikkei and WSJ reporting Beijing's intelligence apparatus may have been involved in cultivating ties to the chipmaker and Caixin detailing the Singapore-based executive's business network; Taiwanese chip suppliers say the fallout has had limited direct impact on TSMC so far.

stories.headline: China's October exports jump 35.2% as AI-related trade surges
stories.summary: China's exports rose 35.2% year-on-year in October to $412.3 billion while imports jumped 41.6%, beating forecasts as AI-related shipments such as chips and computing equipment surged in value even as car exports slowed; Caixin commentary argues the export boom reflects strengthening AI-driven demand for Chinese machinery and industrial components beyond semiconductors.

stories.headline: AI tool helps Wuhan disciplinary officials crack a corruption case
stories.summary: A large language model flagged anomalies in a Wuhan corruption case involving a firm with no registered capital tied to 116 projects, illustrating how Chinese anti-graft agencies are increasingly deploying AI to detect irregularities in local government dealings.

stories.headline: Alibaba's chip unit T-Head eyes Hong Kong IPO
stories.summary: Alibaba's semiconductor division T-Head is exploring a public listing, with the company saying more than 60% of its computing capacity already serves customers outside the Alibaba group as it seeks new capital for expansion.

stories.headline: Toyota overhauls China supply chain to compete in EV race
stories.summary: Toyota is moving beyond its traditional Japanese supplier network to source EV parts from local Chinese companies in an effort to cut costs and keep pace with fast-moving domestic rivals, while leaning on its hybrid technology edge in the interim.

stories.headline: Taiwan coast guard monitors Chinese ships after radio standoff off eastern coast
stories.summary: Taiwan's Coast Guard said it is continuing to track a Chinese coast guard vessel that broadcast sovereignty claims over Taiwan during a radio confrontation near Orchid Island, which the Taiwanese crew rejected before the Chinese ship withdrew further offshore.

stories.headline: CATL targets 6,000 battery-swap stations for passenger cars by 2027
stories.summary: Battery giant CATL plans to build 5,000 urban and 1,000 highway battery-swap stations across 297 Chinese cities by 2027, a push that could see it overtake EV maker Nio in station count.

China.gaps: Could not retrieve recent, distinct coverage from Sixth Tone, China Media Project, China Daily, Xinhua, CGTN, Yicai Global, or Pandaily beyond the AI-product items already in the feed; Global Times, China Daily, Xinhua and CGTN coverage of the APEC/trilateral summit was referenced only via other outlets' citations of their statements, not directly verified.

Gulf & Middle East.overview: Coverage across Gulf and Israeli outlets is dominated by escalating Iran-US-Gulf tensions in the Strait of Hormuz, intensified Israeli strikes on Gaza drawing international condemnation, and Israel's prolonged post-election coalition battle between Netanyahu and Gadi Eisenkot. Business titles are tracking resilient UAE/Saudi economic indicators even as the regional conflict disrupts trade and investment.

stories.headline: Fifth tanker in 24 hours catches fire in Strait of Hormuz after hitting mines
stories.summary: Iran's navy said another oil tanker caught fire on Saturday after striking a naval mine while attempting an unauthorized transit of the Strait of Hormuz, the fifth such incident in a single day, as the IRGC separately claimed to have shot down a US Predator drone over Qeshm Island.

stories.headline: US shoots down Iranian drones headed for Bahrain, denies radar strike claim
stories.summary: US Central Command said it intercepted two Iranian one-way attack drones launched toward Bahrain, denying Tehran's claim it had struck a US early-warning radar there in what would be the first such attack on the kingdom in two months.

stories.headline: US Navy removes commanders of warships deployed against Iran over 'loss of confidence'
stories.summary: The US Navy has dismissed several ship commanders, including the captain of a destroyer deployed against Iran, citing a loss of confidence in their leadership amid the ongoing conflict.

stories.headline: Israeli strikes on Gaza's Nasser Medical Complex draw widespread international condemnation
stories.summary: The UAE condemned Israeli air strikes on the Nasser Medical Complex in Khan Younis, joining diplomats from 18 Muslim-majority countries and the EU in demanding accountability and immediate humanitarian access for Gaza.

stories.headline: Saudi Arabia executes former child protester Jawad Qureiris
stories.summary: Rights groups have condemned the secret execution of Jawad Qureiris, a man arrested as a child protester, calling it part of a pattern of using capital punishment to silence dissent.

stories.headline: Netanyahu renews unity government push as Eisenkot dismisses it as 'political spin'
stories.summary: Benjamin Netanyahu is pressing for a national unity government while haredi parties weigh joining Gadi Eisenkot's rival coalition effort instead, with Eisenkot's camp accusing Netanyahu of insincerity since formal coalition talks are already under way.

stories.headline: Fitch maintains UAE's high-grade credit rating and expects GDP growth this year
stories.summary: Ratings agency Fitch reaffirmed the UAE's high-grade sovereign credit rating and projected economic growth for 2026 despite regional conflict-related disruption.

stories.headline: Saudi assets under management set to surpass $400bn by 2027, Fitch says
stories.summary: Fitch projects Saudi Arabia's assets under management will exceed $400 billion next year, driven by private fund expansion and a strong domestic investor base, with the kingdom's AUM pool remaining the largest and most resilient in the GCC.

Gulf & Middle East.gaps: Could not verify recent coverage from Iran International within the allowed search window; Reuters, AP, FT, NYT, The Economist and BBC block search so only feed-supplied items could be used for them, and none relevant to this beat were provided.

Africa.description: Africa politics, economy and business coverage.
Africa.overview: Coverage clusters around instability and governance stories (DRC jihadist violence, Burkina Faso crackdown, CAR protests, South Sudan's first elections) alongside major economic and trade moves (Angola's De Beers stake bid, Kenya's foreign-dominated retail sector, France-Algeria trade escalation) and the continental fallout from Microsoft's global cloud outage.

stories.headline: ADF attack kills at least 44 in eastern DR Congo
stories.summary: Islamic State-linked ADF fighters killed at least 44 people in a fresh raid in eastern DRC, just days after a separate attack by the group killed 66 people in North Kivu.

stories.headline: Angola seeks 10% stake in De Beers as Anglo American exits
stories.summary: Angola's mines ministry says it wants a 10% holding in De Beers as part of Anglo American's planned sale of the diamond producer, with Namibia reportedly seeking a similar stake.

stories.headline: Microsoft's global cloud outage exposes Africa's reliance on Big Tech
stories.summary: An 18-hour Microsoft outage disrupted South African institutions including Eskom, Absa and FlySafair, while a related piece noted Kenyan banks and insurers lost email access for over 15 hours, exposing deep dependence on one US cloud provider.

stories.headline: Burkina Faso issues arrest warrants for about 20 exiles, including journalists
stories.summary: Ouagadougou issued warrants targeting exiled journalists, activists, a former minister and ex-military officers on terrorism-related charges.

stories.headline: France pushes EU to probe Algeria's trade blockade
stories.summary: Paris has asked the European Commission to investigate Algeria over an alleged near-total freeze on French imports, escalating a bilateral trade dispute to the EU level.

stories.headline: Protesters march in Bangui over rising cost of living and arrests
stories.summary: Hundreds protested in the Central African Republic's capital against soaring fuel prices and the arrest of five civil society leaders.

stories.headline: Foreign investors tighten grip on Kenya's $23bn retail sector
stories.summary: Following Quickmart's oversubscribed IPO, US and UK investors now control roughly 60% of Kenya's supermarket industry even as low-cost Chinese retailers push into the market.

stories.headline: Trump names pastor with no diplomatic experience as ambassador to DRC
stories.summary: South Carolina preacher John Mark Burns has been picked to fill a long-vacant ambassador post as Washington deepens its push for access to Congo's cobalt.

Africa.gaps: No usable recent material could be found for Reuters, AP, BBC, FT, NYT or WSJ (search is blocked for these and no feed items were supplied); The Continent's site returned only archive and about pages rather than a specific recent story.

Media.overview: Media-industry coverage this week centers on turbulence inside major legacy newsrooms following the midterms and the Skydance/Warner-CBS consolidation, with Status and Puck offering the most granular reporting on executive and talent upheaval at CNN, CBS and The New York Times. Separately, FT flags financial strain at Trump Media, Nieman Lab and Poynter cover policy fights over platform payments and press freedom, and Hollywood trades converge on James Gunn's abrupt DC Studios exit.

stories.headline: Trump Media group stares down $1bn debt crunch as bitcoin bet fades
stories.summary: FT reports that a plunge in Trump Media's shares and in cryptocurrency prices could force the Truth Social parent to sell assets or take on expensive new debt to manage a looming $1 billion obligation.

stories.headline: CNN's Contract Cliff
stories.summary: Status reports that top CNN talent including Brianna Keilar and Clarissa Ward face uncertain futures as their contracts near expiration under Skydance, with network boss Mark Thompson also still without a deal, and details how Kara Swisher's exit followed a threat from Elon Musk after he invested in parent company Skydance.

stories.headline: CBS News faces credibility questions and a high-profile exit
stories.summary: Poynter examines veteran anchor Scott Pelley's assertion that CBS News has lost credibility, a charge landing just as Status separately reported that 'Face the Nation' boss Mary Hager, a 35-year CBS veteran, is leaving the network amid a wider wave of Skydance-driven buyouts.

stories.headline: Newsmax's Russian Roulette
stories.summary: Status reports that Newsmax's coverage of a Melania Trump-brokered ceasefire evacuation in Ukraine descended into internal chaos, with staffers raising security concerns after a correspondent accused Russia of using the access as a propaganda opportunity.

stories.headline: The Times' Talent Trap
stories.summary: Status reports that a wave of video and podcast talent departures from The New York Times has overshadowed the paper's push to become a video powerhouse, prompting leadership to quietly try to lure back a former star.

stories.headline: James Gunn denies 'Man of Tomorrow' needs sweeping changes amid DC Studios exit fallout
stories.summary: Variety reports that James Gunn used social media to knock down rumors tying his departure from DC Studios to concerns over the upcoming Superman sequel, saying no one at Skydance had even seen the film.

stories.headline: Indonesia's new copyright bill would force Google and Meta to pay to aggregate news
stories.summary: Nieman Lab reports that Meta, TikTok and Google testified against a proposed Indonesian copyright law this week that would require digital platforms to pay local news publishers for aggregating their content.

stories.headline: What a Democratic-controlled Congress could do to protect press freedom
stories.summary: Poynter outlines how, within 48 hours of Democrats winning control of both chambers, Senator Richard Blumenthal moved to demand FCC records as part of a broader push to use new congressional power on press-freedom issues.

Media.gaps: CJR's items in the feed window were limited to a single roundup post rather than a distinct news story; WSJ, NYT, and The Guardian yielded only the feed items already listed since those outlets block web search.
